reports.title: Cain Donald: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: Planning of discharge from detention under the Mental Health Act at Ashurst PICU directly into the community
Evidence suggested that during the period immediately prior to Mr [name redacted] death, staff of the CRHTT did not implement specific instructions to supervise Mr Donald taking his medication

The evidence revealed deficiencies in the way Mr [name redacted] discharge was planned and executed, specifically that his family and the Probation Services were not properly engaged in the discharge planning process when they were considered important mitigations in any risk Mr Donald posed to himself
concerns.hazard: inadequate risk mitigation through family and probation involvement

links.explanation: Both reports highlight weaknesses in the trust's discharge planning processes that could leave patients unsafe when leaving inpatient care. The earlier report cites unclear communication and risk review, while the later report notes missing family and agency involvement in discharge from a PICU.
links.earlier_quote: Planning for discharge. The evidence indicated the move towards and importance of shorter periods of admission and planning for discharge into the community.
